title: Build a wall
goal: I can use a fraction wall to find equal fractions. I can compare fractions and add and subtract them.

learn.intro: A fraction wall shows one whole cut into equal parts. A longer piece of the wall is a greater fraction. To compare fractions, look at where the pieces end.

example.problem: Which is greater, 5/8 or 3/4? Use the fraction wall.
steps: Shade 5/8 on the row of eighths.
Shade 3/4 on the row of quarters.
The end of 3/4 lines up with the end of 6/8.
6/8 is more than 5/8, so 3/4 is greater.

howto.title: How to compare and add fractions
steps: Make the parts the same size. Use the wall.
To add or subtract, change both to the same bottom number.
Add or subtract the top numbers. Keep the bottom number.

try.explanation: 2/3 = 8/12 on the wall. 7/12 is less than 8/12, so 7/12 < 2/3.

example2.problem: What is 1/2 + 1/4? Use the fraction wall.
steps: On the wall, 1/2 is the same length as 2/4.

items.text: Use the fraction wall to fill in the blanks.
items.explanation: Line up the rows. 1 third is the same length as 2 sixths and 4 twelfths. 2 thirds is 4 sixths and 8 twelfths. 5 sixths is 10 twelfths.

items.text: Write the fraction of each shape that is shaded.
items.explanation: The bottom number is the number of equal parts in the whole shape. The top number is the number of shaded parts. A: 3 of 8. B: 4 of 6. C: 7 of 10. D: 2 of 5.

items.text: Which shapes are cut into EQUAL parts? Circle the letters.   {circ:A|B|C|D}
items.explanation: A fraction needs equal parts. A has 4 equal parts and C has 6 equal sectors. B and D have parts of different sizes.

items.text: Circle <, = or > in each part.
items.explanation: (a) Same bottom number: 5 parts are more than 3 parts. (b) Thirds are larger pieces than quarters. (c) 2/4 = 4/8. (d) 3/4 = 9/12 and 5/6 = 10/12, and 9 is less than 10.
Write each one in sixths: 5/6, 2/6, 3/6, 4/6. The order of the tops is 2, 3, 4, 5. So the order is 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 5/6.

items.text: Fill in the blanks.
items.explanation: When the bottom numbers are the same, add or subtract the top numbers and keep the bottom number. (d) 1 whole is 10/10, and 10/10 - 3/10 = 7/10.

items.text: Change to the same bottom number. Then fill in the blanks.
A cake is cut into 12 equal slices. Ali eats 3 slices. Ben eats 4 slices.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ali and Ben eat {b}/12 of the cake.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Ben eats {b}/12 more of the cake than Ali.

items.text: Look at the number line from 0 to 1. It is cut into equal steps.
items.explanation: There are 8 equal steps, so each step is 1/8. A is 3 steps from 0: 3/8. B is 5 steps: 5/8. C is 7 steps: 7/8. D is 4 steps: 4/8, which is half of the line.

items.text: Fill in the blanks to make equal fractions.
items.explanation: Multiply or divide the top and the bottom by the same number. (a) 4 × 3 = 12, so 3 × 3 = 9. (b) 5 × 2 = 10, so 2 × 2 = 4. (c) 1 × 5 = 5, so 2 × 5 = 10. (d) 6 ÷ 2 = 3, so 8 ÷ 2 = 4.
When the parts are the same size, only the top numbers are added. The bottom number stays 8. 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8.

items.text:
Look at the fractions with bottom number 12. List every one between 1/3 and 2/3.
{ll}
items.explanation: 1/3 = 4/12 and 2/3 = 8/12. The twelfths between 4/12 and 8/12 are 5/12, 6/12 and 7/12. The fractions 4/12 and 8/12 are not between.

items.text: I am a fraction equal to 2/5. My bottom number is 9 more than my top number. Which fraction am I? {b}/{b}
items.explanation: Equal fractions of 2/5 are 4/10, 6/15, 8/20. The gap between bottom and top is 3, 6, 9, 12. The gap is 9 for 6/15. Check: 15 - 6 = 9.
items.hint: Write fractions equal to 2/5. Look at the gap each time.

items.text: A jug is full of juice. Mei drinks 1/4 of the jug. Ali drinks 1/3 of the jug.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Together they drink {b}/12 of the jug.

items.hint: Change quarters and thirds into twelfths first.

items.text:
Beyond Level 3: Adding fractions with top number 1.
Write each fraction as a sum of 2 fractions that each have top number 1.
items.hint: Take away the first fraction. What is left over?

items.text: A whole bar is filled with exactly 6 pieces. The pieces are 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 of the bar. How many of each?
items.explanation: Write everything in eighths: a half is 4, a quarter is 2, an eighth is 1. The 6 pieces must make 8 eighths. With no halves: 2 quarters (4) and 4 eighths (4) make 8. Using 1 half is not possible with 6 pieces: the other 5 pieces would have to make 4 eighths, but each is at least 1.
items.hint: Eighths are the smallest. Most of the 6 pieces must be small.

items.text: Colour the bar. Draw lines in 1/2 of the bar. Draw dots in 1/3 of the bar. Leave the rest white.

parts.label: b
parts.text: That is the same as 1/{b} of the bar.

items.explanation: 1/2 of the bar is 6 parts and 1/3 of the bar is 4 parts. 6 + 4 = 10 parts are coloured, so 2 parts are white. 2/12 is the same as 1/6.
items.hint: 1/2 of 12 parts is 6 parts. How many parts for 1/3?

items.text: Make up a fraction story about a pizza cut into 8 equal slices. The answer to your story must be 5/8.

answer.text: Answers vary. Example: Ali eats 3/8 of a pizza and Mei eats 2/8 of it. Together they eat 5/8 of the pizza.

items.explanation: Check that your fractions all have the same bottom number, and that the story gives 5/8. In the example, 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8.
items.hint: Pick 2 fractions with bottom number 8 that add up to 5/8.

items.text: Write the fraction that is shaded. {b}/8
items.explanation: The bar has 8 equal parts and 5 are shaded. The fraction is 5/8.

items.text: Fill in the blank. 2/3 = {b}/12
